Grid

CSS Grid-based layout system for creating two-dimensional grid layouts with auto-fit, named areas, and responsive column control.

Basic Grid

Use .zak-grid with .zak-grid-item children and grid-template-columns to define columns.

Grid Item 1
Grid Item 2
Grid Item 3
Grid Item 4
Grid Item 5
Grid Item 6
HTML
<div class="zak-grid" style="grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 1rem;">
  <div class="zak-grid-item">Item 1</div>
  <div class="zak-grid-item">Item 2</div>
  <div class="zak-grid-item">Item 3</div>
  <div class="zak-grid-item">Item 4</div>
  <div class="zak-grid-item">Item 5</div>
  <div class="zak-grid-item">Item 6</div>
</div>

Auto-fit Grid

Use auto-fit or auto-fill with minmax() to create responsive grids that automatically adjust the number of columns based on available space.

Auto-fit 1
Auto-fit 2
Auto-fit 3
Auto-fit 4
Auto-fit 5
HTML
<div class="zak-grid" style="grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)); gap: 1rem;">
  <div class="zak-grid-item">Auto-fit Item</div>
  <div class="zak-grid-item">Auto-fit Item</div>
  <div class="zak-grid-item">Auto-fit Item</div>
</div>

Grid Areas

Use named grid areas with grid-template-areas for complex layouts with semantic naming.

Header
Sidebar
Main Content
Footer
HTML
<div class="zak-grid" style="
  grid-template-areas:
    'header header header'
    'sidebar main main'
    'footer footer footer';
  grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr 1fr;
  grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto;
  gap: 0.5rem;
">
  <div class="zak-grid-item" style="grid-area: header">Header</div>
  <div class="zak-grid-item" style="grid-area: sidebar">Sidebar</div>
  <div class="zak-grid-item" style="grid-area: main">Main Content</div>
  <div class="zak-grid-item" style="grid-area: footer">Footer</div>
</div>

CSS Reference

HTML
.zak-grid {
  display: grid;
}

.zak-grid-cols-1 { grid-template-columns: repeat(1, 1fr); }
.zak-grid-cols-2 { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); }
.zak-grid-cols-3 { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); }
.zak-grid-cols-4 { grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); }
.zak-grid-cols-6 { grid-template-columns: repeat(6, 1fr); }
.zak-grid-cols-12 { grid-template-columns: repeat(12, 1fr); }

.zak-gap-sm { gap: 0.5rem; }
.zak-gap-md { gap: 1rem; }
.zak-gap-lg { gap: 1.5rem; }
.zak-gap-xl { gap: 2rem; }

.zak-place-items-center { place-items: center; }
.zak-place-items-start { place-items: start; }
.zak-place-items-end { place-items: end; }
.zak-place-content-center { place-content: center; }

Accessibility

  • CSS Grid maintains DOM order for screen readers — visual reordering with grid-auto-flow: dense can break reading order
  • Ensure grid items contain meaningful content that reads logically without CSS
  • Use semantic HTML elements within grid areas (e.g., <header>, <nav>, <main>)
